status: frozen before new parser execution; researcher-authored development controls, not independent test data
purpose: Separate field correctness, abstention and whole-record correctness for document-assisted discovery/confirmation

reference_semantics.actor_object: canonical lowercase head lemmas, NOT full Rust identities or source-resolved symbols
reference_semantics.action: canonical lowercase predicate lemma for the embedded target action where applicable; coordination evaluates the first action only, not full sentence coverage
reference_semantics.polarity: positive or negative for target action, not outer reporting verb
reference_semantics.force: assertion/report/requirement/conditional; assertion is textual assertion, NOT independently verified implementation
reference_semantics.condition: none or explicit direction between named predicates; not temporal or deontic verification

baseline: Dependency-only transitive-clause proxy, not SRL: root VERB, one active nsubj+dobj or passive nsubjpass+by-agent pobj; direct neg; all fields abstain for coordination/subclauses or root report/state/require/demand. No case-specific identifiers or gold access. Simple accepted clauses have force assertion and condition none.
metrics: Per field and pooled: total, answered, correct, wrong, abstained; coverage=answered/total; selective_exact=correct/answered (null if zero); unconditional_exact=correct/total. Also full-record exact and per-family counts. No weighted score, no statistical/generalization claim.
checks: unique ids and exact field sets
all-abstain yields zero coverage, undefined selective accuracy
duplicate/missing IDs and invalid fields rejected
limits: Same researcher designs controls and baseline from known failure classes. New wording only, not blind/held-out. No cross-validation, provider verification or Rust ground truth. Do not tune rules after results; any revision needs new protocol. Reference labels are hypotheses for bounded controls, not independent annotations. No performance or refactoring benefit claim.
